doc.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Growing up in San Francisco, job discrimination, winning the grammar school drum contest
summary: Alley says hiring was racially closed (no streetcar or bus jobs) so he red capped and shined shoes; he became a drummer by winning a grammar school contest for free lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: When you grew up in San Francisco, I would guess it was different than it is now.

All together different. I can tell you some reasons why. One reason, when I first grew up in Francisco there were two unions, there wasn’t one union, and when I got out — the reason I became a musician, when I got out of school, why it was hard to get a job at different places, in those days, because I couldn’t get a job on the streetcars, buses or stores, it was kind of a racial problem.

Not on streetcars, buses, none, so I red capped and then I shined shoes. The reason I became a musician is because in grammar school they had a contest, when they started band in grammar school.
